subject: Dedicated commit throughput rate floor & benchmark protocol
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@vantedgehealth.com>, VantEdge Procurement <procure@vantedgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit - proposed rate floor & benchmark protocol

Hi Lisa / VantEdge team,

Following our call last week, attaching a concise proposal for the dedicated GPU pool commit and an accompanying benchmarking protocol so we have a shared acceptance criteria for throughput guarantees. High-level summary: 

- Proposed reserved commit: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (pool) dedicated for production workload.
- Baseline throughput (rate floor): 45,000 tokens/sec aggregated (sustained) across pool; equivalent to ~5.6k tokens/sec/GPU for our baseline model (redwood-13B-quant).
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms for 1k-token requests under steady-state batching policy.
- Overage: requests above reserved concurrency will be allowed at a 1.5x per-token price until capacity scales.
- Discount profile: 6m commit -> 18% discount off list, 12m -> 27% (see modeling).

Attached: ratefloor-modeling.xlsx (pricing bands) and bench-protocol.md (step-by-step harness we run). Key asks from your side: confirm which model variant we benchmark (13B vs 70B), desired warm/cold cache behavior (do you want KV-cache cold-start accounted?), and whether you require p99 guarantees.

Proposed benchmark window: May 18-20 (remote run with access to a short-lived load agent we provide). If that works, we'll schedule a dry-run May 17.

If agreeable, we'll follow with an SOW + DocuSign for the commit.

Thanks — looking forward to alignment.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: ratefloor-modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: bench-protocol.md (text)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - proposed rate floor & benchmark protocol

Sergio — quick internal thoughts before we push to VantEdge: 

- The 45k tokens/sec rate floor looks defensible for 8 GPUs on the 13B quant path, but we should frame the commitment bands by effective T/S per GPU, not raw GPU count. That prevents mismatch if they later ask to switch model families.
- Strongly recommend we offer a 3-tier discount ladder by committed tokens/sec (e.g., 35k, 45k, 60k) instead of strictly time-based only. Time-based gives them leverage to lock shorter term with deeper discounts.
- Measurement caveat: bench-protocol.md must specify warm-up (10k tokens) and a sustained 15-minute window for steady-state. Also call out whether we simulate KV-cache reuse or realistic production prefix mixing — those drastically change throughput.

I'll draft the SOW language around the overage pricing and the rollback policy (if rate floor fails on acceptance we offer pro-rated credits). Lauren — can you confirm legal on the rollback/credit clause?

—Ben

(On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 09:12 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote: "Following our call...")

From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@vantedgehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: VantEdge Procurement <procure@vantedgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - proposed rate floor & benchmark protocol

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the proposal and the attachments. A few clarifying questions before we approve the benchmark window: 

1) Model variant: we intend to run real traffic on a 13B family for baseline, but reserve the right to switch to a 70B variant for higher accuracy later. We need a clear mapping in the SOW of how tokens/sec per-GPU maps across those model families.

2) Measurement specifics: please confirm the benchmark harness steps include:
   - Cold start followed by a 20-minute warm-up, then a 30-minute steady-state run.
   - Controlled batch-size profile (we will share a small sample of our real request-size distribution).
   - Whether cache-priming (KV cache hits) will be pre-loaded to the same distribution we expect in prod.

3) Latency SLAs: p95 < 220ms is reasonable for 1k tokens; we'd like p99 as an optional gated metric (we can accept higher p99 if we see consistent behavior and a credit schedule).

4) Legal/Procurement: please send the SOW + DocuSign; we've attached a short doc with a few standard procurement questions (see attached). Also confirm whether your overage rate can be capped for the first month post-commit as we ramp.

We are available for the May 18-20 window but would prefer remote runs only. Please share the load-agent IP allowlist and any monitoring endpoints you'll publish.

Lisa Chen
Director of Platform Engineering
VantEdge Health
mailto:lisa.chen@vantedgehealth.com

Attachment: VantEdge-SOW-questions.pdf (procurement Qs)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@vantedgehealth.com>, VantEdge Procurement <procure@vantedgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 19:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - proposed rate floor & benchmark protocol

Lisa — thanks, good questions. Quick internal-summary and action items: 

- Model mapping: we'll include a table in the SOW that maps tokens/sec per-GPU for 13B/70B/Redwood-XL variants (we'll quote both quantized and full-fp baselines).
- Benchmark changes: we'll update bench-protocol.md to reflect a 20-min warm-up + 30-min steady-state window. We'll also add an explicit cache-priming step (scripted preload) and require them to provide a sample request-size histogram 48h before the run.
- Latency metrics: p50/p95 will be hard SLAs; p99 will be an optional gated metric with a credit schedule (e.g., > p99 baseline triggers partial credit threshold).
- Discount/offers: propose the three-band commit (35k/45k/60k tokens/sec) with the following example pricing bands: 6m (14/18/22% discounts), 12m (22/27/33%). We can cap overage for month one at 1.25x per-token price as a ramp protection.

Next steps I will own:
- Update bench-protocol.md and ratefloor spreadsheet and send an SOW draft to procurement by EOD Wednesday.
- Share load-agent IPs and the monitoring read-only dashboard link ahead of the dry-run.
- Draft SOW clause for rollback credits and the gated p99 schedule for legal review.

If this aligns I will issue the DocuSign SOW (link) and schedule the dry-run for May 17.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: bench-protocol.md (updated draft will follow)
Attachment: ratefloor-modeling.xlsx (updated draft will follow)
